questions.q: Let $x = \dfrac{m}{n} ( m, n$ are co-prime natural numbers) be a solution of the equation $\cos \left(2\sin^{- 1}x\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}$ and let $\alpha, \beta ( \alpha > \beta )$ be the roots of the equation $mx^{2} - nx - m + n = 0$. Then the point $( \alpha, \beta )$ lies on the line
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\cos \left(2\sin^{- 1}x\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Let, $\sin^{- 1}x = \theta$

$⇒ \cos \left(2\theta\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$⇒ 1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$⇒ \dfrac{8}{9} = 2\sin^{2}\theta$

$⇒ sin\theta = \pm \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{2}{3}$

It is given that $m$ and $n$ are co-prime natural numbers,

$⇒ m = 2, n = 3$

Also, $mx^{2} - nx - m + n = 0$.

$⇒ 2x^{2} - 3x - 2 + 3 = 0$

$⇒ 2x^{2} - 3x + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2x^{2} - 2x - x + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2x\left(x - 1\right) - \left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(2x - 1\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 1, \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 1, \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Out of the given options, \left(1, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ lines on $5x + 8y = 9$.

$

questions.solution:
We have,& $\cos^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3x} + \cos^{- 1}\dfrac{3}{4x} = \dfrac{π}{2}, x > \dfrac{3}{4} . . . \left(i\right)$

$∴ \cos^{- 1}$\dfrac{3}{4x} = \sin^{- 1}\dfrac{16x^{2} - 9}{4x}~

Put in~equation~ \left(i\right)$~we get,~

$⇒ \cos^{- $1}\dfrac{2}{3x} + \sin^{- $1}\dfrac{16x^{2} - 9}{4x} = $\dfrac{π}{2} . . . \left(ii\right)$~

We know~$\sin^{- 1}x + \cos^{- 1}x = $\dfrac{π}{2}

From equation~ \left(ii\right)$~we get,~

$⇒ $\dfrac{2}{3x} = \dfrac{16x^{2} - 9}{4x}

$⇒ $\left(\dfrac{8}{3})2 = 16x^{2} - 9 \left(∵ x \ne 0\right)$

$⇒ 16x^{2} = $\dfrac{64}{9} +$9 = $\dfrac{145}{9}

$⇒ x^{2} = $\dfrac{145}{144}

$⇒ x = \dfrac{145}{12}$

questions.q: Let $y = f  \left(x\right)$~represent a parabola with focus  \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2},$0\right) and directrix $y = - $\dfrac{1}{2}.Then~$S = \left\{x \in \mathbb{R}: \tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{f  \left(x\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\left(\ssqrt{f\left(x\right) + 1}\right)\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}\right:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of parabola with focus& $( - \dfrac{1}{2}, 0 )$~and directrix~$y = - \dfrac{1}{2}$~is:

\left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 = \left(y + $\dfrac{1}{4}\right)

$⇒ y = \left(x^{2} + x\right)$

Put~$f ( x ) = y = x + x^{2}$~in~$S$,

$\tan^{- 1}\s$sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}$\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1} = $\dfrac{π}{2}

$⇒ 0 ≤ x^{2} + x + 1 ≤ 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + x ≤ 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Also,

~$x^{2} + x ≥ 0 \ldots \left($2\right)$

By~ \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left($2\right)$, we have

$x^{2} + x = 0 ⇒ x = 0, - 1$

$S$ contains $2 element.

$= \cos^{- 1}\left\{\dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{4}{5}\right\}$

$= \cos^{- 1}\left\{\dfrac{9}{50} + \dfrac{8}{25}\right\}$

$= \cos^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{π}{3}$

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation& $\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1} = \dfrac{π}{4}$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} + x} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1} = \dfrac{π}{4}$

For equation to be defined,

for~$\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x \left(x + 1\right)}$,~

$x^{2} + x ≥ 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + x + 1 ≥ 1 . . . . \left(1\right)$

And, from domain of~$\sin^{- 1}$\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1},~$x^{2} + x + 1 ≤ 1 . . . . \left(2\right)$

$∴$~from \left($1\right) & \left(2\right)$~only possibility that the equation is defined is

$x^{2} + x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, - 1$

at~$x = 0$,~$\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1} =0 + \dfrac{π}{2} \ne \dfrac{π}{4}$

and at~$x = - 1$,~$\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 1} =0 + \dfrac{π}{2} \ne \dfrac{π}{4}$

None of these values satisfy

$∴$ Number~of roots$= 0

$

options: $n ( S ) = 2$~and only one element in~$S$ is less then~$\dfrac{1}{2}$
$n ( S ) = 1$~and the element in~$S$ is more than~$\dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $0 < x < 1$

$2\tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}\right) = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\right)$

Put~$x = \tan \left(\theta\right); 0 < \theta < \dfrac{π}{4}$

$2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - tan\theta}{1 + tan\theta}\right) = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}\right)

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1}\left($\tan \left(\dfrac{π}{4} - \theta\right)\right) = \cos^{- 1} ($\cos 2$\theta )

$2\left(\dfrac{π}{4} - \theta\right) =$2$\theta$⇒ $\theta = \dfrac{π}{8}

Put~\theta = \tan^{- 1}$x$~we get,

$x = tan$\dfrac{π}{8}$∴ x = $\sqrt{2} -$1 ≃ 0 . 414 < \dfrac{1}{2}

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$S = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{3} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{7} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{13} + \ldots \ldots$ up to$10$~terms.

$S = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2 - 1}{1 + 1 . 2}\right) + \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{3 - 2}{1 + 2 . 3}\right) + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{4 - 3}{1 + 3 . 4}\right) + \ldots \ldots + \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{11 - 10}{1 + 11 . 10}\right)

$⇒ S = \left(\tan^{- 1}$2 - \tan^{- 1}1\right) + \left(\tan^{- 1}3 - \tan^{- 1}2\right) + \ldots \ldots + \left(\tan^{- 1}11 - \tan^{- 1}10\right)$

$⇒ S = \tan^{- 1}11 - \tan^{- 1}1$

$⇒ S = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{11 - 1}{1 + 11 \cdot 1}\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{10}{12}\right)

$∴ \tan ( S ) = \dfrac{5}{6}$

$

questions.solution:
Let& $\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}x}{α} = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}x}{β} = k$

i.e.~$\sin^{- 1}x = k\alpha$~and~$\cos^{- 1}x = k\beta$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}x + \cos^{- 1}x = k \left(\alpha + \beta\right)

i.e.~$k\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}

$⇒ k = $\dfrac{π}{2\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}

Now~\dfrac{2\pi\alpha}{\alpha + \beta} =$4k$\alpha =$4\sin^{- 1}x$

So~$\sin \left(\dfrac{2\pi\alpha}{\alpha + \beta}\right) = \sin \left(4\sin^{- 1}x\right)$

$= 2\sin \left(2\sin^{- 1}x\right)\cos \left($2\sin^{- 1}x\right)$

$= 2\sin \left(\sin^{- 1}2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)$

$= 2\sin \left(\sin^{- 1$11}2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\r$right)\cos \left(\cos^{- 1}\left($1 - 2x^{2}\right)\right)$

$= 4x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} \left($1 - 2x^{2}\right)$

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 16\left(\sec ^{-1} x\right)^2+\left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} x\right)^2 \\ & \operatorname{Sec}^{-1} x=a \in[0, \pi]-\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\} \\ & \operatorname{cosec}^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{2}-a \\ & =16\left[a^2+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-a\right)^2\right]=16\left[2 a^2-\pi a+\frac{\pi^2}{4}\right] \\ & \max ]_{a=\pi}=16\left[2 \pi^2-\pi^2+\pi \frac{2}{4}\right]=20 \pi^2 \\ & \min ]_{a=\frac{\pi}{4}}=16\left[\frac{2 \times \pi^2}{16}-\frac{\pi^2}{4}+\frac{\pi^2}{4}\right]=2 \pi^2 \\ & \operatorname{Sum}=22 \pi^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If for some $\alpha, \beta ; \alpha \leq \beta, \alpha+\beta=8$ and $\sec ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} \alpha\right)+\operatorname{cosec}^2\left(\cot ^{-1} \beta\right)-36$, then $\alpha^2+\beta$ is_______.

questions.q: For $k \in \mathbb{R}$, let the solutions of the equation $\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(xcot\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) = k, 0 < \left|x\right| < \dfrac{1}{2}$~be $\alpha$ and $\beta$, where the inverse trigonometric functions take only principal values. If the solutions of the equation $x^{2} - bx - 5 = 0$~are $\dfrac{1}{\alpha2} + \dfrac{1}{\beta2}$~and $\dfrac{α}{β}$, then $\dfrac{b}{k2}$& is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(xcot\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) = k$

Now simplifying~$\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}x\right) = \cos \left(\cos^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right) = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}$

So, $\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(xcot\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) = k$

becomes $\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(xcot\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\right)\right) = k$

And now solving $\cot \left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right) = {cotcot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}$

So,~$\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(xcot\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\right)\right) = k$~becomes~

$\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1 - x^{2}}\right)\right) = k$

Now solving~$\cos \left(\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1 - x^{2}}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1 - 2x^{2}}{1 - x^{2}}$

So,~$\dfrac{1 - 2x^{2}}{1 - x^{2}} = k$

$⇒ 1 - 2x^{2} = k^{2} \left(1 - x^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(k^{2} - 2\right)x^{2} = k^{2} - 1$

$⇒ x^{2} = $\dfrac{k^{2} - 1}{k^{2} - 2}

So, roots are~$\alpha = $\sqrt{\dfrac{k^{2} - 1}{k^{2} - 2}}$⇒ {α}^{2} = $\dfrac{k^{2} - 1}{k^{2} - 2}

And~$\beta = - $\sqrt{\dfrac{k^{2} - 1}{k^{2} - 2}}$⇒ {β}^{2} = $\dfrac{k^{2} - 1}{k^{2} - 2}

Now finding~\dfrac{1}{\alpha2} + \dfrac{1}{\beta2} =$2 \left(\dfrac{k^{2} - 2}{k^{2} - 1}\right)~and~\dfrac{α}{β} = -$1$

So, sum of roots of~$x^{2} - bx - 5 = 0$~will be~=\dfrac{1}{\alpha2} + \dfrac{1}{\beta2} + \dfrac{α}{β} =$b$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2 \left($k^{2} - 2\right)}${k^{2} - 1} -1 = b ⋯ \left($1\right)$

Product of roots of~$x^{2} - bx - 5 = 0$~will be~=\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha2} + \dfrac{1}{\beta2})\dfrac{α}{β} = -5$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(k^{2} - 2\right)}{k^{2} - 1}\left(-1\right) = - 5$

$⇒ 2k^{2} - 4 = 5k^{2} - 5$

$⇒ 3k^{2} = 1 ⇒ k^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3}⋯ Putin \left($1\right)$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{2\left(k^{2} - 2\right)}{k^{2} - 1} -1 = 5 - 1 = 4$

$\dfrac{b}{k2} = \dfrac{4}{13} =12$

$

questions.q: For $n \in \mathrm{N}$, if $\cot ^{-1} 3+\cot ^{-1} 4+\cot ^{-1} 5+\cot ^{-1} n=\frac{\pi}{4}$, then $n$ is equal to_____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \cot ^{-1} 3+\cot ^{-1} 4+\cot ^{-1} 5+\cot ^1 n=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{3}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{4}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{5}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{46}{48}\right)+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{23}{24}\right)+\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}=\tan ^{-1} 1-\tan ^{-1} \frac{23}{24}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{n}=\tan ^{-1} 1-\tan ^{-1} \frac{23}{24} \\ & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{n}=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\frac{23}{24}}{1+\frac{23}{24}}\right) \\ & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{n}=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{1}{24}}{\frac{47}{24}}\right) \\ & \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{n}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{47} \\ & n=47\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If& $S = \left\{x \in \mathbb{R}: \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + 2x + 2}\right) - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4}\right\}$~then~$\mathop{∑}_{x \in S}\left(\sin \left(\left($x^{2} + x + 5\right)\dfrac{π}{2}\right) --\cos \left(\left(x^{2} + x + 5\right)\pi\right)\right)~is equal to~_________ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + 2x + 2}\right) - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + x + 2}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4} + \sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 1}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + x + 2}\right) =$\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\right)

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + x + 2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{x^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 1}

$⇒ $\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2} + x + 2} = \dfrac{x + 1}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{x^{2} + 1}}

$⇒ \left($x + 1\right)\left(\sqrt{2}\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} - \sqrt{x^{2} + x + 2}\right) =$0$

$⇒ x = - 1$~or~\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 2} = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}

Now solving,~\sqrt{x^{2} + x + 2} = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}~we get,

$x^{2} + x + 2 = 2 \left(x^{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ x^{2} - x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, x = 1$~{rejected as $x = 1$~will not satisfy the~given equation}

Hence,~$S = \left\{0, 1\right\}$

Now solving,

$\mathop{∑}_{n \in S} \left(\sin \left($x^{2} + x + 5\right)\dfrac{π}{2} --\cos \left(x^{2} + x + 5\right)\pi\right)

=\left(sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} -$\cos 5\pi $+sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} -$\cos 5\pi\right)$

$= 1 - \left(-1\right) + 1 - \left(-1\right) = 4$

$

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\tan \left\{\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + r + r^{2}}\right)\right\}$ is equal to_______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{n \to \infty}\tan \left(\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + r\left(r + 1\right)}\right)\right)

$= \lim_{n \to $\infty}\tan \left(\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{r + 1 - r}{1 + r\left(r + 1\right)}\right)\right)$

$= \tan \left(\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n} \left[\tan^{- 1} \left($r + 1\right) - \tan^{- $1}\left($r\right)\right]\right)$

$= \tan \left(\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(\tan^{- 1}\left(n + 1\right) - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)

$= \tan \left(\dfrac{π}{4}) =$1$

$$
